messages.content: I keep saying yes to plans I don't actually want to go to.
Honestly, that's a really common people-pleasing pattern. What usually makes you say yes even when you don't want to?
I think I'm scared people will stop inviting me if I say no too much.
That fear makes sense, honestly, but the opposite usually happens - people actually respect boundaries more than blind availability over time.
So how do I start saying no without feeling guilty?
Start small, honestly - practice on lower-stakes invitations first, and remind yourself that a kind, clear no doesn't require an elaborate excuse to be valid.
